b: Staying consistent on TikTok sounds simple enough. But between coming up with ideas, filming, editing, and writing captions, posting at a good time is usually the step that slips.
So, can you schedule TikTok posts? Yes, both in TikTok itself and with a tool like Buffer. TikTok's own scheduler has a few limitations worth knowing before you start, though!

In this guide, I'll walk through how to schedule TikTok posts on desktop and mobile, how to schedule photo posts, what to do when the schedule option doesn't show up, and how I'd choose between TikTok's scheduler and Buffer.
You can schedule TikTok videos natively from 15 minutes to 30 days ahead via TikTok Studio on desktop or the TikTok Studio mobile app.
Once a post is scheduled in TikTok, you can't edit it. You can only delete it and upload it again.
Buffer lets you schedule TikTok posts, edit posts until the moment they go live, schedule photo posts, and crosspost the same video to Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts.
To use a trending sound, schedule with Buffer's Notify Me option and add the sound in TikTok when your reminder comes through.

Can you schedule posts on TikTok?

Yes. On desktop, TikTok lets you schedule a video from 15 minutes to 30 days ahead, and the TikTok Studio app on mobile has a schedule option too. Once a post is scheduled on TikTok, you can't edit it (only delete it).
Here are TikTok's scheduling rules in one place:

How to schedule TikTok posts on desktop
You have two options on desktop: TikTok Studio in your browser, or a scheduling tool like Buffer. I'll start with TikTok's own.
How to schedule TikToks on desktop with TikTok Studio
Scheduling works on any TikTok account, so there's nothing to set up first. Here's how:
Go to tiktok.com on a computer and click Upload to open TikTok Studio. (You could also just head straight over to tiktok.com/tiktokstudio.)
Click the Upload button on the top left, then choose photos or video.
Upload your photos or video. Add a caption and edit your cover.
Under Settings, turn on Schedule, pick a date and time up to 30 days out, and click Schedule.
TikTok's scheduler is free and built-in, so it's a good fit if you only post to TikTok and plan within the month. But there are a few trade-offs:
You can't edit a scheduled post. Fixing a typo in the caption means deleting the post and uploading it again.
It only posts to TikTok, so if the same video is going to Instagram Reels or YouTube Shorts, you'd schedule those separately.
You can't schedule more than 30 days out, so if you batch content a quarter at a time, you'll keep coming back to top it up.
If any of those get in your way, a social media management tool can cover them. Here's how it works in Buffer.
How to schedule TikTok videos on desktop with Buffer
With Buffer's TikTok scheduler, you can edit a post right up until it goes out, plan further than 30 days ahead, and send the same video to other social media platforms from one place.
Sign up for Buffer. The free plan lets you connect up to three channels (TikTok included!) with 10 scheduled posts per channel at a time.
Click Add Channel, choose TikTok, and authorize Buffer.
Pro tip: Log in to TikTok in the same browser first. Buffer will connect whichever TikTok account you're already signed in to.
Click Finish Connection, and you're ready to schedule.
Then, to schedule a TikTok post with Buffer:
Click + New > Post and select your TikTok account. You can select other channels here too if you want to crosspost.
Upload your video or images. The preview on the right shows how the post will look on TikTok.
Write your caption. You can add up to five hashtags, and if you're stuck on a caption, Buffer's AI Assistant can help you draft or tighten it.

When you're ready to publish, at the bottom of the composer, choose Automatic or Notify Me. Automatic publishes the video for you at the scheduled time. Notify Me sends a push notification to your phone at the scheduled time. Tap it, and you'll finish posting in the TikTok app. This is the one to use when you want a trending sound or a poll, or something you can only do natively in TikTok.

Pick when it goes out: Next Available adds it to your next queue slot, Prioritize (paid plans) moves it to the top of the queue, Set Date and Time lets you pick a specific slot, and Now posts it straight away.
Pro tip: If you want more channels or advanced features to run your social media strategy from one place, all Buffer's paid plans come with a 14-day free trial.
How to schedule TikTok posts on mobile

On your phone, you can schedule with the TikTok Studio app or the Buffer app. Both work on iPhone and Android. The main TikTok app doesn't have a documented scheduling option yet, though there have been reports of TikTok testing one.
How to schedule TikTok posts with the TikTok Studio app
The TikTok Studio app is TikTok's companion app for creators, and you can download it from the App Store or Google Play.
Download TikTok Studio and log in to your TikTok account.
Tap Upload and add your video.
Tap Schedule post and choose a date and time.
The same rules apply as on desktop: up to 30 days ahead, and no editing once a post is scheduled.
How to schedule TikTok posts with the Buffer app
The Buffer app works on iPhone and Android, with the same publishing options as desktop.
Open Buffer and tap Compose a Post or the + icon.
Choose your TikTok account, upload your video, write your caption, and pick your thumbnail.
Tap the green arrow button on the top right, then add the post to the next available slot, set a specific date and time, or share it now.
Tap Schedule Post, and you're good to go.
How to schedule TikTok photo posts
You can schedule a photo post (TikTok's carousel format) in TikTok Studio the same way as a video: upload your photos instead, then turn on Schedule.

In Buffer's web app, create a post the same way as above and upload up to 10 images instead of a video. Images need to be JPG or WebP (PNG and HEIC files will be converted to JPG for you) and no larger than 1080 x 1920 pixels (full specs).
Buffer is the better fit when the same carousel is also going to Instagram or LinkedIn, since you can schedule them together.
Two limits to know about: photo posts only work from Buffer's web app for now, not the mobile app, and Buffer takes up to 10 images while TikTok allows up to 35.

Why can't I schedule posts on TikTok?
If the Schedule option isn't showing up, it's usually your device or the time you picked. Here's what to check:
Your device. Scheduling isn't available on TikTok's mobile website, and the main TikTok app doesn't support it. Use tiktok.com on a computer or the TikTok Studio app.
The time you picked. TikTok only accepts times between 15 minutes and 30 days from now.
If neither fixes it, you can schedule the post in Buffer instead!
How to edit, delete, or check a scheduled TikTok

Posts scheduled in TikTok Studio, either on mobile or desktop, can't be edited at all. To make a change, you'll have to delete it and upload it again (so it's worth keeping a copy of your caption somewhere!).
In Buffer, scheduled TikToks sit in your queue and calendar. You can open any of them and change the caption, thumbnail, time, or publishing mode up until it goes out.
To check that a post went live, look for TikTok's notification or check your profile. In Buffer, published posts move to the Sent tab of your Publish dashboard.
A few habits that make scheduled TikToks work better
Scheduling takes care of the posting. These three habits help them get seen.
1. Schedule for when your audience is around
Your TikTok analytics show when your followers are most active, so that's the first place I'd look.
To see when your followers are active on TikTok:
From your profile, tap the TikTok Studio button.
Tap Viewers in the top menu and scroll down to Most active times.

If your account is new and there isn't much data yet, our analysis of 7.1 million TikTok posts is a good starting point. In that study, Sunday at 9 a.m. was the single best slot, followed by Monday at 1 p.m. and Sunday at 1 p.m., and Saturday was the strongest day overall.
2. Be around to reply to comments

Early comments are a good signal to the TikTok algorithm, and scheduling means you might not be at your phone when a post goes live. Buffer's Community pulls your TikTok comments into one inbox alongside nine other networks, so you can reply quickly from wherever you are!
3. Keep your original files and captions

This matters most with TikTok's own scheduler, since fixing anything means deleting and re-uploading. A folder containing the final video and a doc with the caption saves you from having to rewrite it from memory.

How far in advance can you schedule a TikTok?

Up to 30 days with TikTok's own scheduler, and no sooner than 15 minutes from now. With Buffer, TikTok's 30-day window doesn't apply, because Buffer holds the post and publishes it at the time you set. On Buffer's free plan, you can have 10 posts queued per channel at a time.
How many followers do you need to schedule on TikTok?
None. Any TikTok account can schedule posts, with no follower minimum and no need for a Business account. Older guides still mention a 10,000-follower requirement, but that rule no longer applies.
Where is the schedule button on TikTok?

On desktop, upload your video in TikTok Studio, scroll to Settings, and turn on Schedule. In the TikTok Studio app on iPhone or Android, it's the Schedule post option in the upload flow. If you don't see it, check you're in TikTok Studio rather than the main TikTok app.
Can you edit a scheduled TikTok?
Not with TikTok's scheduler. You can delete a scheduled post, but you can't change its video, caption, or time. In Buffer, you can edit a scheduled post until it publishes.
Do scheduled TikToks get fewer views?
TikTok hasn't said that scheduling affects reach, and I haven't seen evidence that it does. What tends to matter more is posting when your audience is active and replying to early comments.
Can you schedule TikTok posts with trending sounds?

In TikTok's own scheduler, yes, as long as the sound is available to your account (Business accounts are limited to commercially licensed music). In Buffer, use Notify Me and add the sound in the TikTok app when your reminder comes through.
Can I schedule to TikTok and Instagram at the same time?
Not with TikTok's scheduler, which only posts to TikTok. In Buffer, you can select your TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube accounts in the same post and adjust each caption before you schedule.
Is there a free TikTok scheduler?
Yes, two. TikTok's built-in scheduler is free for every account, and Buffer's free plan lets you connect up to three channels (TikTok included) with 10 scheduled posts per channel at a time.
